Other `429`s — the per-minute brakes and daily budgets described with the
endpoints below — carry `Retry-
After` whenever the refusal knows when it\nlifts, which is the ordinary case. Treat it as a hint that is usually there\nrather tha
n a guarantee: a refusal that reaches you without one still needs\nyour backoff, so **never** block waiting for a header that may

not come.

## Endpoints

Each endpoint is fully documented — request and response schemas, examples,
and an interactive playg

round — under **Endpoints** in the sidebar.

**Catalog** — discover the IDs everything else takes:

|

| `GET /me` | The account behind the key |
| `GET /organizations` | The organizations the caller belongs to — where
`organizationId` comes from. A key is bound to one organization and only ever sees that one |\n| `GET /projects` | Projects the k
ey can access (optionally `?organizationId=`) |\n| `GET /projects/{projectId}/servers` | The project's saved MCP servers |\n| `GET
/projects/{projectId}/servers/{serverId}/revisions` | A server's stored revisions, newest first: captures of its tools and server
info, recorded whenever they change (`?limit=&cursor=`) |\n| `GET /projects/{projectId}/servers/{serverId}/revisions/{revisionNum
ber}` | One revision: every tool's definition and the server info it reported. Fields listed in `droppedFields` were too large to
store, so they are unknown, not absent |\n| `GET /projects/{projectId}/servers/{serverId}/revisions/{revisionNumber}/diff` | What
changed since the revision before, or since `?from=`: tools added, removed and changed, and server info changes with both values.

lient}` | Read, edit, or delete a client. The path segment takes a client **name or ID** |\n| `POST /projects/{projectId}/clients/

rojectId}/clients/{client}/duplicate` | Copy a client's current config into a new client |\n| `GET /chat-sessions` | Chat sessions

**Project environments** — the named execution bundles (one host, optionally a
stand
alone server group, optionally pinned skills and plugin versions) that eval\nsuites and goals run against. Reads need project memb
ership; **every write\nneeds project admin**. Writes are revisioned: pass the `revision` you last read\nback as `expectedRevision`

, and a stale value returns `CONFLICT` (409) instead
of overwriting a concurrent edit.

| Endpoint | What it does |
| - | - |\
n| `GET`, `POST /projects/{projectId}/environments` | List environments (`?includeArchived=true` to include archived ones), or cre
ate one |\n| `GET`, `PATCH /projects/{projectId}/environments/{environmentId}` | Read one environment, or edit it (send `null` to
clear `serverAttachmentId`, `skillSelection`, or `pluginVersionIds`) |\n| `GET /projects/{projectId}/environments/{environmentId}/
resolve` | Preview the host config, closed server set, and pinned plugin versions this environment resolves to right now |\n| `POS
T /projects/{projectId}/environments/{environmentId}/archive` | Archive it — reversible, and frees the name for a new one |\n| `PO
ST /projects/{projectId}/environments/{environmentId}/restore` | Restore an archived environment |\n\nArchive and restore are expl
icit sub-actions rather than a `DELETE` because the\nrow is kept and restore has real semantics: it re-checks the name and drops\n
plugin pins whose version no longer exists.\n\n**Server diagnostics & primitives** (`/projects/{projectId}/servers/{serverId}/...`

):

er require an OAuth grant? |\n| `POST .../tools` | List the server's tools |\n| `POST .../tools/call` | Execute a tool; returns th
e MCP `CallToolResult` plus additive `durationMs`, and `authChallenge` when the result asks for sign-in (see [Sign-in challenges](

he MCP `GetPromptResult` verbatim |\n| `POST .../resources` | List the server's resources |\n| `POST .../resources/read` | Read on

**Eval runs** (`/projects/{projectId}/...`):

| Endpoint | What it does |
| - | - |
| `POST .../eval-suit
es` | Author-only: create a suite + its test cases from `name` + `serverIds` + a default `model` + `tests`, WITHOUT running it; re
sponds `201` + `suiteId`. Each test's case body is an ordered `steps` array (prompt / toolCall / interact / assert); per-test `mod
el`/`provider`/`runs` are optional and fall back to suite defaults |\n| `POST .../eval-runs` | Create a run from a `suiteId` (reru
n; `serverIds` optional — defaults to the suite's saved servers) or `suiteName` + inline `tests` + `serverIds` (new suite). `envir
onmentId` (requires `suiteId`) runs against one of the suite's attached environments instead. Responds `202` + `runId` |\n| `PATCH
.../eval-suites/{suiteId}` | Edit suite settings, including `environmentIds` — the project environments the suite runs against (n
on-empty array sets/replaces, `null` clears) |\n| `PATCH .../eval-suites/{suiteId}/schedule` | Enable/disable scheduled runs; `env
ironmentId` pins which environment they launch |\n| `GET .../eval-runs/{runId}` | Run status, result, and summary — poll until ter
minal. Carries `gateWaiver`: the audited override in force over this run's gate, or `null` |\n| `GET .../eval-runs/{runId}/gate` |
The stored suite quality-gate report for this run (`passed` / `failed` / `non_gateable` / `not_configured`). `not_configured` is
a 200 report, never a missing route. A deployment that predates the evaluator answers `422 FEATURE_NOT_SUPPORTED` |\n| `GET .../ev
al-runs/{runId}/decision-summary` | **Start here when a run did not pass.** The canonical run decision contract: the verdict and w
here it came from, counts labelled with the population they count, the run's own verdict decision, and per-trial diagnostics with
the user-value chain, the first failed stage, the failure category, evidence scoped to that stage, and one next action (paginated)
|\n| `POST .../eval-runs/{runId}/gate-waivers` | Override a **failing** run's release gate until `expiresAt` (required, future, m
ax 30 days out), with a `reason` (required, max 500 chars). Manage tier. Does NOT change the run's `result` — the run keeps its ve
rdict and the waiver is reported alongside it. `409` when one is already in force, returning the existing waiver |\n| `GET .../eva
l-runs/{runId}/gate-waivers` | The waiver in force over a run, or `null`. Readable by anyone who can view the run |\n| `DELETE ...
/eval-runs/{runId}/gate-waivers/{waiverId}` | Revoke a waiver, putting the gate back. Idempotent — a second call reports the origi
nal revocation rather than restamping it |\n| `GET .../eval-runs/{runId}/iterations` | Per-iteration results: tool calls, token us
age, latency (paginated) |\n| `GET .../eval-runs/{runId}/iterations/{iterationId}/trace` | Full trace: messages + expected-vs-actu

al analysis |
| `GET .../eval-suites/{suiteId}/runs` | Recent runs for a suite, newest first |
